findings.title: Negative offset passed to Django QuerySet slice will crash at runtime
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset` is negative. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing — this raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually incorrect. Any request that triggers this path will result in a 500 error.

findings.title: BasePaginator change allows negative offsets for all subclasses when is_prev is true
findings.body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` in `BasePaginator.get_result` removes the lower-bound protection for ALL paginator subclasses (Paginator, DateTimePaginator, etc.) when `cursor.is_prev` is true. A malformed or adversarial cursor string with a negative offset (e.g., via `Cursor.from_string`) will cause a Django AssertionError on the queryset slice. This is a regression affecting all existing paginators, not just the new OptimizedCursorPaginator.

findings.title: Unrelated and dangerous pagination feature smuggled into spans buffer PR behind weak authorization check
findings.body: The `optimized_pagination` query parameter enables `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`, which allows negative offsets. The authorization check (`request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`) is bypassed if the `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is used elsewhere without this gate. More importantly, this feature is broken (negative Django slicing crashes) and appears unrelated to the stated PR purpose of span buffer optimization. This looks like an attempt to introduce a backdoor pagination mechanism.

findings.title: Silent span eviction via zpopmin with no observability
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, `zpopmin` silently removes the oldest spans (by end_timestamp_precise score). There is no metric, log, or return value indicating that eviction occurred. This makes it impossible to detect data loss in production. The evicted spans are permanently lost with no way to alert on or measure the frequency of this event.

findings.title: Hardcoded eviction limit of 1000 in Lua script is not configurable and differs from Python max_segment_spans=1001
findings.body: The Lua script hardcodes the eviction threshold at 1000, while the Python `SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts `max_segment_spans=1001` (now unused). This creates a discrepancy: the effective limit changed from 1001 to 1000, and the Python parameter is now dead code that misleads future maintainers into thinking the limit is configurable.

findings.title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl as segment_page_size due to positional argument mismatch
findings.body: The `__reduce__` method returns `(SpansBuffer, (self.assigned_shards, self.span_buffer_timeout_secs, self.span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, self.redis_ttl))`. The constructor signature is `__init__(self, assigned_shards, span_buffer_timeout_secs, span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, segment_page_size, max_segment_bytes, max_segment_spans, redis_ttl)`. So `self.redis_ttl` (3600) is passed as `segment_page_size` instead of as `redis_ttl`. This means after pickling/unpickling (e.g., in multiprocessing), the buffer will have `segment_page_size=3600` and `redis_ttl=3600` (default), which happens to work by coincidence but is fragile and incorrect.

findings.title: KeyError if end_timestamp_precise is missing from span event
findings.body: The code accesses `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` without a default or existence check. If a span event is missing this field (e.g., from an older producer or malformed message), this will raise a KeyError and crash the consumer. The `cast(SpanEvent, ...)` provides no runtime protection. A `.get()` with a fallback or explicit validation would be safer.

findings.title: Misleading comment about negative offset support in Cursor class
findings.body: The added comment says 'Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios' but the code `self.offset = int(offset)` already accepted negative values before this change. The comment implies a behavioral change that doesn't exist here — the actual (broken) negative offset handling is in the paginator. This comment may mislead future readers into thinking the Cursor class itself provides safety for negative offsets.

findings.title: max_segment_spans parameter is now dead code
findings.body: The `max_segment_spans` parameter is still accepted in `__init__` and stored as `self.max_segment_spans`, but the code that used it (the span count check during `_load_segment_data`) has been removed. The parameter is now unused dead code that will confuse maintainers and appears in the constructor signature as if it still has an effect.
